fx.formula: one-way = (sell - mid) / mid where mid = (buy + sell) / 2
fx.warning: Snapshot of a published board. It is not a quote, not the PBOC fixing, and not a forecast. The bank's actual execution rate governs.

_meta.note: Costs are decomposed so that published items are computed and unpublished items stay blank. No tax amount is computed for a person whose facts are unknown.

lines.label: Bank FX margin on RMB to USD purchase (one way)
lines.basis: BOC board: spot sell 6.6903 vs spot buy 6.6622; midpoint 6.67625
lines.note: The margin is half the bid/ask spread. It is the bank's compensation and is separate from commission.

lines.label: Round-trip FX margin if you convert twice
lines.basis: Same board; buy and sell spread
lines.note: Converting RMB to USD and back costs roughly double the one-way margin. Avoid unnecessary round trips.

lines.label: PBOC central parity vs BOC customer rate
lines.basis: Central parity 6.7188 (S10) vs BOC mid 6.67625 (S08)
lines.note: The fixing is a reference rate, not a tradeable price. Do not present the gap between the fixing and a bank rate as a customer cost.

lines.label: BOC cross-border telegraphic transfer commission
lines.basis: 0.1% of the remitted amount, minimum CNY 50, maximum CNY 260
lines.note: Note 1 of the tariff allows negotiated, discounted or local variations.

lines.label: BOC cable / telecommunications charge
lines.basis: CNY 150 per transfer outside Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan; CNY 80 within
lines.note: Published base schedule; local variation possible under note 1.

lines.label: Intermediary (correspondent) bank deduction
lines.basis: SWIFT chains may pass through one or more correspondents, each of which may deduct a fee
lines.note: No official schedule applies. It depends on the routing banks and the charge code used. Left blank rather than guessed.

lines.label: Receiving bank incoming-wire fee
lines.basis: Set by the U.S. receiving bank and account tier; not verified for this user
lines.note: Ask your U.S. bank for its published incoming international wire fee and whether it is waived for your account tier.

lines.label: AML identity verification above CNY 5,000 / USD 1,000
lines.basis: PBOC order 2025 No. 11, Article 34, effective 2026-01-01
lines.display: No published fee; may add time
lines.note: This is a compliance step, not a charge. It can delay a transfer and may trigger document requests.

lines.label: China IIT on wage and salary income
lines.basis: Progressive 3% to 45% for comprehensive income
lines.note: Applies when earned, not when converted. If already withheld and paid, conversion adds no wage tax.

lines.label: China IIT on transfer of assets (property, equity)
lines.basis: Flat 20% of taxable gain
lines.note: For housing, if the original value cannot be documented, a 1% deemed assessment on the transfer amount may apply (S18).

lines.label: China IIT on FIE dividends to a foreign individual
lines.basis: 20% from 2026-09-01; the former exemption is repealed
lines.note: A treaty may reduce the rate, but relief is fact-specific and requires analysis (S25).

lines.label: China VAT on sale of housing
lines.basis: 3% of the full amount if held under 2 years; exempt at 2 years or more, from 2026-01-01
lines.note: Residential housing only; non-residential property has different treatment.

lines.label: China IIT exemption for sole home held 5+ years
lines.basis: Exempt if the property was self-used for 5+ years and is the family's only home
lines.note: Requires a written undertaking and supporting family/housing documents.

lines.label: China inheritance tax
lines.basis: No current inheritance-tax statute was located in this session
lines.note: Do not assume zero. The absence of a located statute is not proof that no charge applies to a specific estate.

lines.label: U.S. income tax on the underlying income
lines.basis: U.S. citizens are taxed on worldwide income
lines.display: Ordinary rates / capital rates as applicable
lines.note: Moving money does not create income by itself, but it does not erase the tax on income already earned either.

lines.label: Section 988 foreign currency gain on converting RMB
lines.basis: Disposition of nonfunctional currency is a section 988 transaction; gain is ordinary income
lines.display: Ordinary income on RMB appreciation between acquisition and conversion
lines.note: Requires a USD basis for each tranche of RMB. Without acquisition records the gain cannot be computed.

lines.label: Foreign tax credit for China tax paid
lines.basis: Nonrefundable credit for foreign income taxes paid or accrued, subject to limitation
lines.note: The credit is limited to U.S. tax on foreign-source income in the relevant basket.

lines.label: FBAR (FinCEN 114) non-filing
lines.basis: Aggregate foreign accounts over USD 10,000 at any time; civil maximums adjusted annually for inflation
lines.display: Up to USD 10,000 per non-willful violation; willful greater of USD 100,000 or 50% of balance
lines.note: Penalty maximums are inflation-adjusted; the figures shown are the published base amounts in the IRS comparison table.

lines.label: Form 8938 non-filing
lines.basis: Thresholds from USD 50,000 (unmarried, living in the U.S.) / 200,000 (living abroad); up to USD 10,000 plus USD 10,000 per 30 days after notice, maximum USD 60,000
lines.note: Separate from and additional to the FBAR.

lines.label: Form 3520 for a foreign gift or bequest over USD 100,000
lines.basis: Receipt of more than USD 100,000 from a nonresident alien individual or foreign estate
lines.note: A gift is generally not taxable income to the recipient, but the information return is still required.

lines.label: State income tax
lines.basis: State rules vary; not researched per state
lines.note: Residency and domicile facts are unknown.

lines.label: U.S. exit tax
lines.basis: Not applicable to a citizen who remains a citizen; expatriation rules are a different fact pattern
lines.note: Included to close a common misconception: converting or transferring funds is not an expatriation event.

lines.label: Penalty for evasion (逃汇) or illegal FX purchase (非法套汇)
lines.basis: Fines up to 30% of the amount; 30% up to the equivalent amount if serious
lines.note: This dwarfs every lawful fee. It is the real 'conversion penalty' risk to avoid.

lines.label: Penalty for private FX trading
lines.basis: Confiscation of gains plus fines up to 30%, or 30%-100% if serious
lines.note: Applies to underground banks and private brokers.

lines.label: Penalty for illegal cash carriage
lines.basis: Warning and fines up to 20% of the amount; customs rules may also apply
lines.note: Cash above the permitted amount can be detained or confiscated.

lines.label: Delay and opportunity cost
lines.basis: Approval timelines, bank processing and rate movement
lines.note: No published service standard exists for SAFE approval of an individual property transfer.

scenarios.title: Already-taxed documented salary, converted lawfully
scenarios.assumption: The entire balance is post-tax salary already reported in the U.S., and the RMB was acquired at the same exchange rate as conversion.
scenarios.us_tax: 0 incremental on principal; section 988 gain may still arise if RMB appreciated
scenarios.why: Conversion is not itself a taxable event; the tax attaches to the income when earned.
scenarios.label: ILLUSTRATION ONLY — facts unknown

scenarios.title: Section 988 gain if RMB appreciated 1%
scenarios.assumption: USD 400,000 of RMB was acquired when RMB was 1% weaker; converted now.
scenarios.us_tax: Gain 4,000 taxed as ordinary income: about 960 at 24%, 1,280 at 32%, 1,480 at 37%
scenarios.why: Section 988 treats the currency disposition as ordinary gain or loss measured by rate movement.
scenarios.label: SENSITIVITY ILLUSTRATION — not a personal estimate

scenarios.title: Property gain taxed at 20%
scenarios.assumption: USD 400,000 sale proceeds with a USD 280,000 documented cost basis and no exemption.
scenarios.china_tax: 20% of 120,000 = 24,000, plus VAT only if held under 2 years
scenarios.us_tax: U.S. tax on the gain, with a foreign tax credit for the China tax subject to limitation
scenarios.why: Asset-transfer income is taxed at a flat 20% in China.
scenarios.label: ILLUSTRATION ONLY — no property facts supplied

scenarios.title: Property sale with no original-value proof (deemed 1%)
scenarios.assumption: USD 400,000 proceeds and no complete original-value documentation.
scenarios.us_tax: Depends on basis and gain; credit may be limited
scenarios.why: Where original value cannot be established, the checklist allows deemed assessment at 1% of the transfer amount.
scenarios.label: ILLUSTRATION ONLY

scenarios.title: FIE dividend to a foreign individual
scenarios.assumption: USD 400,000 gross dividend from an FIE to a foreign individual shareholder.
scenarios.china_tax: 20% = 80,000 (40,000 only if a treaty reduces the rate to 10% and relief is granted)
scenarios.us_tax: U.S. tax on the gross dividend with a foreign tax credit subject to limitation
scenarios.why: 2026 No. 27 repealed the old exemption from 2026-09-01.
scenarios.label: ILLUSTRATION ONLY — treaty relief unverified for your facts

scenarios.title: Inheritance received from China
scenarios.assumption: USD 400,000 inheritance from a Chinese relative, already taxed where required.
scenarios.china_tax: No inheritance-tax statute located; transfer still needs SAFE approval and tax clearance on the estate assets
scenarios.us_tax: Not taxable income to the recipient; Form 3520 may be required above USD 100,000
scenarios.why: Inheritances are generally not income in the U.S., but information reporting still applies.
scenarios.label: ILLUSTRATION ONLY — legal conclusion unverified

scenarios.title: Using an illegal route
scenarios.assumption: USD 400,000 moved through a private broker.
scenarios.china_tax: Potential fine 0-30% (120,000) or up to 100% (400,000) if serious, plus confiscation
scenarios.us_tax: Unchanged: U.S. tax and reporting still apply
scenarios.why: The penalty range under the FX Regulations is larger than any lawful fee.
scenarios.label: RISK ILLUSTRATION
